title: Article 51 — Promotion of international peace and security

content.overview: Article 51 directs the State to endeavour to promote international peace and security; maintain just and honourable relations between nations; foster respect for international law and treaty obligations in the dealings of organised peoples with one another; and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
content.glance: Promote international peace and security; just relations between nations; respect for international law and treaties; encourage arbitration of international disputes.
content.study:
Article 51 is the international-relations DPSP. It supports India’s engagement with international law and treaty obligations and peaceful settlement of disputes.

Examination: four heads — peace and security; just relations; international law and treaties; arbitration.

sections.heading: Four heads
sections.body:
(a) Promote international peace and security.
(b) Maintain just and honourable relations between nations.
(c) Foster respect for international law and treaty obligations.
(d) Encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 51 direct?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 51 directs the State to endeavour to (a) promote international peace and security; (b) maintain just and honourable relations between nations; (c) foster respect for international law and treaty obligations in the dealings of organised peoples with one another; and (d) encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

examTips: Peace, just relations, international law/treaties, arbitration.

keyTakeaways: Art 51: international peace, law, treaties, arbitration.
